messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired (PD-8231) -> inference-api-prod-eu: 5xx error rate spike >4% over 3m. Affected route: /v1/generate and /v1/embed. Pager: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8231 :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Paging on-call (ops-mike). Escalation policy: inference-prod -> ops -> eng-lead.

ops-mike: acked in PagerDuty, taking it. Joining bridge in 60s. Can someone put a quick customer-impact note in here?

sre-jen: I'm on the bridge. Quick sanity: checking autoscaler events and recent deploys. Running logs query against inference-runtime pods.

platform-lucia: ping @sales-ella for customer-facing flag. If this is noisy but transient we can avoid broad comms.

sales-ella: seeing a couple support tickets from two midmarket customers about failed completions. No large enterprise flags yet. I'll standby for updates.

ops-mike: initial findings: spike correlates with a sudden increase in 502/504 from runtime frontends -> upstream gRPC pool returning UNAVAILABLE. Latency also up ~2x. Not seeing a rollout in the last 15m.

sre-jen: grabbing logs: ```
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=inference-runtime --since=10m | grep -E "UNAVAILABLE|KVCache|retry" | tail -n 100
# sample: 2026-03-15T14:02:13Z runtime: grpc: failed to dial /10.32.4.9: model-host: UNAVAILABLE
```

platform-lucia: that IP range is the dedicated kvcache pool. Could be connection storm where nodes hit max FDs. infra-bot, can you check host-level metrics (FD usage, connection counts) for the kvcache group?

infra-bot: KV cache fleet host metrics: several hosts show FD > 80%, ephemeral port exhaustion on 10.32.4.6 and 10.32.4.9. Autoscaler hasn't added new kvcache nodes in the last 5m due to scale-up throttle.

ops-mike: plan A: temporarily increase kvcache pool size + bump fd limits on affected hosts. Plan B if that fails: route inference requests to fallback model variant (lower mem) to reduce KV load. Executing Plan A now.

sre-jen: executing rolling restart of kvcache sidecar on the two hotspots (10.32.4.6, 10.32.4.9) with cmds below — doing one at a time: ```
ssh root@10.32.4.6 'systemctl restart kvcache-sidecar' && sleep 30
ssh root@10.32.4.9 'systemctl restart kvcache-sidecar' && sleep 30
```

ops-mike: increased pool target from 12 -> 18 (temporary). Request to autoscaler submitted. Watching 5xx rate.

platform-lucia: putting an autoscaler override to unblock scale-up. Also applying sysctl net.netfilter to lift ephemeral ports temporarily.

sre-jen: 14:06 - 5xx rate dropping to ~1.2%, latency trending down. Customers may see some recovered requests.

ops-mike: note for incident record: root cause likely connection exhaustion on kvcache hosts due to a workload surge + scale-up throttle.

sales-ella: internal update done: "We observed degraded completion rates for ~10-12 minutes for some customers in EU region; engineering is mitigating and rollback unnecessary."

platform-lucia: flagging that autoscaler config had a safety throttle that prevented immediate scale-up when connection errors spiked — filing follow-up to revisit throttle thresholds.

ops-mike: 14:12 - handing off primary ownership to platform-lucia for postmortem and config fix. I'll remain on bridge until they've got a remediation plan. @platform-lucia can you take the incident? :handshake:

platform-lucia: taking it. I'll open the PD ticket and assign root-cause analysis, include autoscaler throttling + host fd limits as action items. Estimated postmortem ETA: EOD.

sre-jen: quick follow-ups: add KV cache connection metrics to the alert rule so next time PagerDuty triggers earlier on FD or connection saturation, not just 5xx rate.

infra-bot: created ticket #INFR-4617 to raise FD limits and add host-level alert.

ops-mike: thanks all. Closing PD acknowledgement once platform-lucia confirms. Final status: mitigation applied, error rate reduced, customer impact limited to ~10-12 minutes, two support tickets opened.

platform-lucia: confirmed, I'll own communication with stakeholders and schedule a small rollback window if we need to test changes. Reassigning ownership to me now.

sre-jen: quick note for postmortem: include a short playbook step for "kvcache FD spike" — how to scale and triage faster.

platform-lucia: got it. I'll include runbook edits. Closing thread for active ops handover; leave comments here for anything urgent. :white_check_mark:
